IR.rationale: A steepening term spread signals better growth expectations and reflation, which favours cyclical non-US equity markets.

B.rationale: Narrowing spreads together with strong high-yield returns mark easy credit and rising risk appetite, which spill over to global equities.

V.rationale: High implied volatility carries a large variance risk premium and tends to precede higher subsequent equity returns as risk compensation.

AP.rationale: US returns lead non-US markets through time-zone lags and slow cross-market information diffusion, so a strong US week carries into foreign indices.

ST.rationale: Weak momentum returns typically coincide with junk rebounds after sell-offs, a state linked to subsequent recovery in broad indices.

FX.rationale: A weakening dollar eases global dollar funding conditions and raises the USD value of foreign equities.

COM.rationale: Rising broad commodity prices signal global demand strength, which benefits cyclical and resource-heavy developed markets.

MC.rationale: Tight financial conditions raise required risk premia, so expected returns are higher going forward.

ENDG.rationale: Recent index performance captures time-series momentum or short-horizon reversal; the model learns the sign.

IR.rationale: Falling intermediate yields relative to policy rates reflect flight-to-quality and growth scares that precede turbulent equity markets.

B.rationale: Widening spreads with falling high-yield prices signal rising default risk and deleveraging, which raises future equity volatility.

V.rationale: Implied volatility contains forward-looking information on realised variance beyond its own lags, and global volatility shocks transmit across developed markets.

AP.rationale: The leverage and volatility-feedback effects make negative market returns precede higher variance.

ST.rationale: High reversal returns indicate expensive liquidity provision, which is characteristic of stressed, volatile markets.

FX.rationale: Yen appreciation together with Australian-dollar weakness marks carry-trade unwinding and global risk-off, which precede volatile equity markets.

COM.rationale: Sharp oil declines signal demand shocks and stress in energy credit, which raise equity uncertainty.

MC.rationale: Elevated financial stress reflects funding strains and uncertainty that persist and raise subsequent realised variance.

ENDG.rationale: Volatility clusters, so high recent realised variance shifts the level of future variance.

IR.rationale: Falling yields relative to the policy rate signal flight to safety and expected easing in response to deteriorating conditions.

B.rationale: Credit deterioration often leads equity drawdowns, since bond markets price default risk early.

V.rationale: High implied volatility widens the return distribution and raises the probability of left-tail outcomes.

AP.rationale: Simultaneous weakness in US and emerging equities signals a global risk-off that propagates to developed non-US markets with lags.

ST.rationale: High reversal profits indicate scarce liquidity provision, a condition under which large drawdowns are more likely.

FX.rationale: Safe-haven yen strength combined with weakness in commodity currencies is a classic signature of carry crashes and equity sell-offs.

COM.rationale: Falling commodity prices signal weakening global demand, which raises the risk of equity losses.

MC.rationale: Financial stress raises crash probability through deleveraging and funding constraints.

ENDG.rationale: Poor recent returns coincide with stress regimes where further large losses are more likely.

IR.rationale: Curve steepening reflects improving growth expectations and reflation, which favour strong equity rallies.

B.rationale: Strong high-yield returns indicate returning risk appetite and credit healing, which often precede equity rallies.

V.rationale: Elevated volatility fattens both tails, and high risk premia make sharp relief rallies more likely.

AP.rationale: Broad strength in US and emerging equities signals a global risk-on that lifts developed non-US markets.

ST.rationale: Momentum crashes happen in rebounds when past losers surge, a state associated with large market gains.

FX.rationale: Dollar weakness combined with commodity-currency strength marks easing global liquidity and risk-on, which boost foreign equities in dollar terms.

COM.rationale: Commodity strength reflects global reflation and demand, which support upside equity outcomes.

MC.rationale: Tight conditions mean depressed prices and high risk premia, from which large gains occur when conditions ease.

ENDG.rationale: Large gains cluster after weak periods as short-horizon rebounds; the model learns the sign.
